title: HB1486 (2020 Regular): RELATING TO GUNS.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Hawaii) (gun-policy Stage 5, Hawaii); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Hawaii text (Introduced, official copy, https://data.capitol.hawaii.gov/sessions/session2020/bills/HB1486_.HTM; sha256 00be9c8ee9c7f70d8898523a4f8899ef2bcab7d5a42c63d835dc0b30cd367a3b)
provenance.note: Introduced text (as filed). Part II (SECTIONS 5-7: HRS 121-34.5, 134-16, 134-17) repeals the ban on possessing, selling or lending electric guns; those sections are mostly struck text and are not quoted. No passage vote recorded. Carried over to 2020; text differs from the 2019 file only in its header line (see check).

SECTION 2 (HRS 134-2): (5) A firearms training or safety course or class conducted by a state certified firearms instructor or a certified military firearms instructor that provides, at a minimum, all of the training of a safety course or class described in paragraph (4) and also provides a total of at least four hours of additional training in:
SECTION 2 (HRS 134-2): (A) Properly carrying concealed and unconcealed weapons in public;
SECTION 3 (HRS 134-9): (2) Six months from the date of issue if the license was issued on an initial or renewal basis after June 30, 2019.
SECTION 3 (HRS 134-9): (5) Also carry on the person an electric gun, as defined in section 134-1, which is intended to be non-lethal by design, whenever the licensee carries a pistol or revolver pursuant to the license.
SECTION 3 (HRS 134-9): (c) If a licensee violates any requirement relating to the license, the chief of police who issued the license shall revoke the license.
